prompt: How does `WeekNav` change the week, when the week is kept in `App`?
hint: Look at what `App` passes as `onChange`.

choices.text: It changes its `monday` prop
choices.why: Props are read-only; changing one would change nothing React watches.

choices.text: It keeps its own copy of the week in a variable and React reads it from there
choices.why: A plain variable is created again on every render, and React never reads it.

choices.text: It calls the function its parent passed down as a prop
choices.why: Right. `App` hands `setMonday` down, and the child calls it with the new Monday.

choices.text: It reloads the page with the week in the address
choices.why: Nothing reloads; addresses are lesson 17's subject.

prompt: Opened in your own browser, the planner probably shows a week with no sessions. Why?
hint: Where does the starting week come from now?

choices.text: It starts at today's week, and the data is in October 2026
choices.why: Right. A few presses of a button reach the data's week.

choices.text: The data failed to load
choices.why: The data is a module; it always loads.

choices.text: Strict mode clears state on load
choices.why: Strict mode does not change what the screen shows.

choices.text: `today()` returns a date in UTC
choices.why: It reads the local date; the week is right, it is just empty.

prompt: Put the steps of an update in order, after "Next week" is pressed.
hint: Only the last of React's steps touches the page.
items: `setMonday` is called with the new Monday
React calls `App` and every component below it
React compares the new tree with the last one
React changes the page where the two differ

prompt: Why can React call a component and throw the result away?
hint: What does rendering change?

choices.text: Because the browser caches every component
choices.why: The browser knows nothing about components.

choices.text: Because components without state are skipped
choices.why: Every component under the change was called, stateless or not.

choices.text: It cannot, since a render reaches the page
choices.why: Strict mode throws away a render on every load in development.

choices.text: Rendering changes nothing
choices.why: Right, as long as components are pure: the page changes only at the commit.

prompt: With strict mode off, how many components were called after one press of "Next week"?
hint: Count the lines after `-- click button Next week`.

prompt: `WeekNav` received the same `onChange` and only a new `monday`. Why was it called again?
hint: What does React compare before rendering a child?

choices.text: Because its props changed
choices.why: That is true here and not the reason: it would have rendered with identical props too.

choices.text: Because its parent rendered
choices.why: Right. React renders every component below the one whose state changed, unless you ask for `memo`.

choices.text: Because a clicked button renders itself again
choices.why: Being clicked does nothing to a component; its parent's state does.

choices.text: Because strict mode was on
choices.why: Strict mode was off for that transcript.

prompt: If `WeekNav` kept the week in its own state instead of `App`, what would a press of "Next week" render?
hint: A state change renders that component and what is below it.

choices.text: Every component, as now
choices.why: Components above or beside the changed one are not rendered.

choices.text: No component, because a child has no state of its own
choices.why: Any component can have state; `Probe` did.

choices.text: `App` and `WeekNav`, but not the cards
choices.why: `App` is above `WeekNav` and would not render.

choices.text: `WeekNav` only, so the summary and the cards would not change
choices.why: Right. Which is why the state lives above every component that reads it.

prompt: Why did every `render` line appear twice on the first load?
hint: Look at what wraps `<App />` in `main.tsx`.

choices.text: A bug in `rendered.ts`
choices.why: The file logs once per call; there were two calls.

choices.text: The page loaded twice because of Vite
choices.why: One load; removing `StrictMode` alone halved the lines.

choices.text: `look` prints every console line twice
choices.why: Without strict mode it printed each once.

choices.text: Strict mode, in development
choices.why: Right. It throws the second result away, to find impure components.

prompt: Which of these does strict mode do? Choose every one.
hint: Three of the four are in the section.

choices.text: Calls each component a second time in development
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Runs effects, cleans them up and runs them again
choices.why: Yes, which lesson 5 uses.

choices.text: Warns about deprecated interfaces
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Renders twice in the production build too
choices.why: No: in a build it does nothing.

prompt: A component adds one item to a list declared outside it every time it renders. What does strict mode make visible?
hint: Two calls, one result kept.

choices.text: Two items per render, so the impurity shows at once
choices.why: Right. That is what the second call is for.

choices.text: No difference: the second call's result is thrown away
choices.why: The result is thrown away; the item it added to the list is not.

choices.text: An error that stops the render
choices.why: Strict mode does not detect the mutation; it makes its effect double.

choices.text: A warning naming the list
choices.why: React cannot see your variable; you see the doubling.

prompt: How many changes did the `MutationObserver` report after "Next week"?
hint: Count the records on the `DOM:` line.

prompt: What kind were all the changes after "Next week"?
hint: The observer printed the type first.

choices.text: Text inside nodes that already existed
choices.why: Right. Every record was `characterData`.

choices.text: New elements added for the new week
choices.why: No element was created or removed.

choices.text: The whole `#root` replaced
choices.why: That happened once, on load.

choices.text: Attributes on the buttons
choices.why: The buttons were untouched.

prompt: Why does keeping DOM nodes, rather than recreating them, matter to a keyboard user?
hint: What does the browser associate with a node?

choices.text: Keyboard events are slower on new nodes
choices.why: Speed is not the issue; what the node remembers is.

choices.text: Screen readers cannot read nodes created after load
choices.why: They read them; the trouble is losing the place the user was at.

choices.text: It does not; only the paint time matters
choices.why: Focus moving away is a real failure for someone without a mouse.

choices.text: A recreated node would lose focus and selection
choices.why: Right. The button you pressed still has focus after the click.

prompt: Why did the word "session" under Organic chemistry change in the new week?
hint: Look at the ternary in `CourseCard`.

choices.text: React rewrites every text node in a card when one changes
choices.why: Only the differing nodes were written; this one differed.

choices.text: The course was renamed
choices.why: The heading did not change.

choices.text: `MutationObserver` reports every word on the line
choices.why: It reports nodes that changed, and this one changed.

choices.text: Zero sessions takes the plural
choices.why: Right. One session became none, and the ternary chose `sessions`.

prompt: After two presses and "Next week", the Statistics probe still said 2. Why?
hint: State belongs to a place in the tree.

choices.text: The count is saved in the browser's storage
choices.why: Nothing was stored; it lived in React.

choices.text: Same type, same place
choices.why: Right. The first card's `Probe` was still there after the render.

choices.text: `Probe` did not render again
choices.why: It rendered, and kept its state.

choices.text: The click went to the wrong card
choices.why: It went where it was aimed.

prompt: With `key={monday}` on `CourseList`, every probe went back to 0 after "Next week". What did the new key do?
hint: A different key is a different component.

choices.text: It sorted the courses by date
choices.why: Keys do not sort anything.

choices.text: React rebuilt the list from scratch
choices.why: Right. Nothing under the old key survived.

choices.text: It set every `count` to `monday`
choices.why: The key never reaches the component as a value.

choices.text: It stopped `Probe` from rendering
choices.why: They rendered, freshly created.

prompt: A form edits one student at a time and should start empty when another student is chosen. With this lesson's tool, what is the least code?
hint: The tool resets a whole subtree at once.

choices.text: `key={student.id}` on the form
choices.why: Right. A new id is a new form, with fresh state.

choices.text: Clear each field when the choice changes
choices.why: That works, and it is one line per field.

choices.text: Reload the page
choices.why: That resets everything else too, and loses the choice.

choices.text: Turn strict mode off
choices.why: Strict mode has nothing to do with resetting.

prompt: Match each change to what happens to `Probe`'s count.
hint: Ask whether the same type stays at the same position.

pairs.left: The parent renders with new props
Strict mode calls the component a second time

prompt: To make React treat a component as a new one, give it a different ___.
hint: The attribute `CourseList` received.

prompt: A component calls `Math.random()` to pick a colour while it renders. In development, what changes compared with production?
hint: How many times is it called, and which result is kept?

choices.text: No change: one call in both
choices.why: Development calls it twice under strict mode.

choices.text: Both colours are drawn, one on top of the other
choices.why: Only one result reaches the commit.

choices.text: React refuses to render it
choices.why: React cannot tell a random number from any other value.

choices.text: It is called twice and one colour is shown
choices.why: Right. The extra call is thrown away; the impurity is that the colour changes on every render anyway.

prompt: Without strict mode, how many `render` lines does one load of the page print?
hint: App, WeekNav, WeekSummary, CourseList, and three of each card.

prompt: Which statement about this lesson's screen is true?
hint: Separate rendering from changing the page.

choices.text: The components with new props rendered, and the rest were skipped
choices.why: All ten rendered.

choices.text: The elements were recreated for the new week
choices.why: No element was recreated.

choices.text: Ten renders, ten text changes
choices.why: Right: every component was called, and the commit wrote only the difference.

choices.text: No component, because the page was already drawn
choices.why: The logs show ten calls.
